stem: A 49-year-old man, medically retired after a chronic illness, presents with about eleven weeks of worsening low-back pain radiating to both legs, which he and his family initially attributed to years of manual work before his retirement. Over-the-counter analgesics have given only partial relief, and he has lost some weight without trying. No prior TB treatment, no known TB contact, no known drug-resistant contact. MRI of the spine shows destruction of two adjacent vertebral bodies with a paraspinal collection, concerning for spinal TB (Pott's disease). CT-guided aspiration of the paraspinal collection was sent for molecular testing, which was positive for M. tuberculosis. Exam: point tenderness over the lower lumbar spine, mild bilateral leg weakness, no bowel or bladder involvement.

patient.occupation: medically retired (chronic illness, formerly manual work)
patient.social_history: Lives with family; longstanding history of manual work attributed as the cause of his back pain
patient.presenting_complaint: Progressive low-back pain radiating to both legs, mild leg weakness, unintentional weight loss
patient.exam_findings: Point tenderness over lower lumbar spine, mild bilateral leg weakness, no bowel/bladder involvement, vertebral body destruction with paraspinal collection on imaging
patient.prior_treatment: Over-the-counter analgesics with only partial relief; no prior TB treatment

distractors: Mechanical back pain from a longstanding occupational manual-work history proposed as sufficient explanation without imaging follow-through
His known degenerative joint disease proposed as the explanation for the leg weakness rather than a spinal cord or nerve root process
ntep_correct_actions: Perform upfront molecular testing (NAAT) directly on the accessible extrapulmonary specimen (the CT-guided paraspinal aspirate) as the first-line microbiological tool, rather than anchoring the workup around culture and histology as the primary reference standard.
who_correct_actions: Perform upfront molecular testing (NAAT) directly on the accessible extrapulmonary specimen (the CT-guided paraspinal aspirate) as the first-line microbiological tool, rather than anchoring the workup around culture and histology as the primary reference standard.
us_correct_actions: Anchor the diagnostic workup for this extrapulmonary presentation around culture and histology as the reference standard, treating molecular testing as a general, conditional adjunct rather than the upfront first-line tool for extrapulmonary specimens.
critical_error_conditions: Attributing the vertebral destruction and new leg weakness entirely to degenerative joint disease and deferring targeted aspirate sampling and molecular testing
expected_divergence_points: Whether upfront molecular testing on the accessible extrapulmonary specimen is the first-line diagnostic tool or culture/histology remains the anchoring reference standard
